newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Aug 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Aug 1.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- More than 20,000 convicted criminals had firearm licences, while 12,470 individuals owned 10 or more firearms, with 62 having between 50 and 648, Safety Minister Sydney Mufamadi said on Thursday.

- Transnet MD Saki Macozoma launched a scathing attack on Transport Minister Mac Maharaj on Thursday, saying his recent statements on the parastatal and its subsidiaries could scuttle the restructuring process.
- International business perceived South Africa as more corrupt than it was a year ago, Transparency International's corruption index showed on Thursday.

- President Nelson Mandela has declined to disclose the contents of a "highly sensitive" letter from Nigerian leader Sani Abacha delivered to him at his Johannesburg home by two envoys on Thursday, saying that confidentiality was essential.
BUSINESS REPORT

- The local gold industry slid into the red for the first time ever in the quarter to June 30, with at least 15 mines, or 40 percent of the industry, producing at a loss and another five mines close to making a loss, analysts said on Thursday.

- Stronger commodity prices, tighter cost control and a small increase in sales volumes boosted Polifin Ltd's full-year attributable earnings 20 percent to 543 million rand on a 14 percent rise in turnover to 3.6 billion rand.
- Wooltru Ltd, the retail conglomerate, has emerged as the surprise suitor for CNA Gallo Ltd's core stationery and news agency business.

- A further 42,000 jobs were shed in South Africa's non-agricultural formal sector during the first quarter of this year, shattering government hopes of creating 252,000 jobs this year, figures released on Thursday by the Central Statistical Service (CSS) showed.
SAKE BEELD
- Business leaders and companies will be asked to testify before the Truth and Reconciliation Commission on the role of business and labour under apartheid at a hearing in November.

- Polifin announced it was planning investments of seven billion rand to expand its production capacity. The chemicals company reported a rise in earnings for the year to June 25, 1997 to 99 cents per share from 83 cents per share in the past year. Attributable income rose to 543 million rand from 454 in the previous year.

- Rand dips below critical 4.60 level but no panic is evident in the market, and even Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals says the local currency's performance is due to the strength of the dollar rather than the weakness of the rand.
- Information technology firm Persetel Holdings Ltd posted better than expected yearly results showing a 52 percent rise in 1996/97 earnings per share to 70.1 cents.
THE STAR
- The 17 million rand highway robbery in which two security guards were killed on Thursday may have been planned with the help of inside information.
- Thousands of families will be left without electricity in Gauteng on Tuesday, when the provincial government sends a tough message to defaulters who don't pay for municipal services.
- Twenty percent of the workforce at Sun City has been retrenched in an attempt to streamline the reportedly cash-strapped entertainment complex.
- More than 20,000 people with convictions for serious crimes might be in possession of firearm licences, Safety and Security Minister Sydney Mufamadi said on Thursday.
